name: VaultSparkStudios.github.io
currentFocus: Session 336 set out to run the arc and deploy, and found the deploy path itself was broken: prune-served-surface had been REFUSING on /evidence/ (added S334) and /how-we-build/ (added S335) because neither page was ever added to the hand-maintained config/served-surface.json, so no deploy of any kind could succeed. The failure was self-planting — the content lane promotes sitemap.xml, so a new route becomes advertised in production on one deploy and only breaks the next one, which is why S334 and S335 both looked like they worked. The entire S335 release had been sitting unserved. Fixed the manifest, added a prune --check that runs the real manifest against the real tree in build:check (proven to fire on the restored regression), and promoted the content lane: /how-we-build/ now returns 200 and the deployed contentLaneHead contains the S335 commit. Then fixed the reason nothing alarmed — deploy-currency measured only deployed-commit-to-tip against a 48h ceiling, a clock hourly cron commits continuously reset, so 34 uptime crons and one stranded release read identically; it now ages a second clock from the oldest undeployed hand-authored commit, classified structurally against the served-surface manifest and evidence graph. Also made api/tt-readiness.json disclose the age of its evidence: it had been stamping a fresh generatedAt over a manifest from 2026-07-07 and holding amber-soak forever on rows nothing ever aged out.
publicNote: Everything the studio shipped on 1 September is now actually live — Season 1, the community wall, the member dashboard, and the new How We Build page, which had been unreachable. The site also gained a check that stops a page being published without being deployable, and its Trusted Types security report now states how old its evidence is instead of implying it is current.
nextMilestone: Founder decision on which member activity becomes publicly readable, then one short migration adding definer projection views for challenge_submissions, game_sessions, point_events and member_achievements — four public tables still render a silent zero to anonymous visitors. Then the manual CANON-053 rendered-pixel review of the surfaces that only now actually serve, and a fresh Trusted Types KV soak so the enforce flip can be decided on real evidence.
blockers: PRIVACY DECISION (founder): four public tables — challenge_submissions, game_sessions, point_events, member_achievements — have no anonymous read path, so /community/, all seven /leaderboards/* and public member profiles render zeros and empty states to signed-out visitors. The fix generalizes the S335 public_leaderboard pattern, but it decides which member activity becomes publicly readable and is escalated rather than applied (D-S336.5).
